properties.name: Jorf Lasfar Thermal Complex
properties.description: Morocco's single largest power station and the backbone of its baseload capacity. Units 1–4 (1,356 MW) are operated by JLEC (TAQA); units 5–6 (700 MW) by ONEE. The plant burns imported coal and is a primary candidate for phased retirement under Morocco's NDC commitments. It shares the Jorf Lasfar industrial port with OCP's phosphate processing complex.

properties.name: Ain Beni Mathar ISCC
properties.description: Africa's first Integrated Solar Combined Cycle plant: a 20 MW parabolic trough solar field paired with a 452 MW gas combined cycle. Located in the Oriental region near the Algerian border. The solar component displaces ~12,000 t CO₂/yr and proved the viability of hybrid solar-thermal at utility scale in North Africa.

properties.name: Tahaddart CCGT
properties.description: Morocco's first independent power producer (IPP) under a BOT contract. Located near Tangier, it receives natural gas via the Maghreb–Europe Gas Pipeline from Algeria. The plant serves as peaking and mid-merit capacity for the northern grid and the Spain interconnect.

properties.name: Mohammedia Thermal Plant
properties.description: Aging heavy fuel oil plant near Mohammedia, between Casablanca and Rabat. Increasingly used as a strategic reserve rather than baseload, given its high operating costs relative to renewables. A candidate for decommissioning or repowering as grid flexibility assets are added.
